content.overview: If the agreed appointment machinery fails, the High Court or Supreme Court (or its designate) appoints. The court looks at existence of the agreement.
content.study: Do not turn a section 11 petition into a mini-trial on merits. Validity and scope go to the tribunal under 16. International commercial arbitration appointment sits in the Supreme Court.

learningObjectives: State the rule recorded for Section 11 Arbitration Act — Appointment.
Separate the points already present in the topic sections.
Do not add a case or section number that is not already in this note.
enhancement.definition: Section 11 provides the statutory mechanism for appointment of arbitrators when the agreed appointment procedure fails. The designated Supreme Court or High Court, as applicable under the section, or a person or institution designated by that court, performs the appointment function within the statutory framework.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Section 11 is concerned with constituting the arbitral tribunal when the parties' agreed mechanism does not operate. The court's role is not to conduct a full merits trial at the appointment stage.
enhancement.statutoryFramework: The Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 — Section 11 Arbitration Act — Appointment
essentialIngredients: The agreed appointment procedure has failed or the statutory trigger for court intervention is met.
A qualifying request for appointment is made under Section 11.
The court applies the statutory appointment framework, including the distinction between international commercial arbitration and other arbitration.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: The appointment mechanism must be read with the parties' agreement and the statutory procedure. Section 11 also contains time-related and application requirements. The nature of the arbitration determines whether the Supreme Court or High Court is the relevant appointing authority under the Act.

examples.title: Failure of agreed appointment
examples.body: Two parties have an arbitration agreement requiring each to nominate one arbitrator, but one party fails to make the nomination after the contractual/statutory trigger arises. The applicant can analyse the Section 11 route to obtain the required appointment.

examples.title: Scope of appointment inquiry
examples.body: A respondent seeks to turn a Section 11 application into a detailed merits trial. The analysis should distinguish the appointment function from the arbitral tribunal's later jurisdictional and merits functions.

enhancement.problemApplication: The contract contains an arbitration clause and a three-member tribunal procedure. One party does not appoint its nominee. Identify the appointment mechanism, the statutory trigger, the appropriate court under the Act, and the limited nature of the appointment-stage inquiry.
keyTakeaways: Section 11 facilitates constitution of the tribunal when appointment machinery fails.
The applicable appointing authority depends on the statutory framework and nature of arbitration.
Appointment proceedings are not a substitute for the arbitral merits process.

notes: Enhancement expanded from migrated baseline using the current statutory structure identified in India Code. Independent legal verification remains a separate gate.

distinctions: Section 11 appointment vs Section 8 referral: appointment constitutes the tribunal; referral moves a judicial action into arbitration.
Section 11 vs Section 16: Section 11 concerns constitution; Section 16 concerns the tribunal's jurisdiction.
enhancement.examAnswerStructure: For 10 marks: purpose → triggers → appointing authority → procedure → limited inquiry. For 16 marks add party-agreement analysis, international-commercial distinction, and relationship with Sections 7, 8 and 16.
